neighbours.label: counterfactual or avoidable-outcome modal: could/would (have) describing what might have happened or been prevented
fire: The accident was tragic because a simple railing could have prevented it.
With better maps, the climbers likely would have found the hut before dark.
Experts say thousands of deaths could have been avoided with early warnings.
If the bridge had been inspected, the collapse would never have happened.
A five-minute check could easily have caught the error in the contract.
Many of these fires could be prevented if people cleared dry brush.
The company argued that profits would have grown if not for the strike.
Looking back, the war could and should have been stopped much sooner.
quiet: The accident was tragic because the railing was broken that night.
With good maps, the climbers found the hut well before dark.
Experts say thousands of deaths were recorded during the heat wave.
When the bridge was inspected, the engineers found a small crack.
A five-minute check caught the error in the contract yesterday.
Many of these fires start in late summer when the brush is dry.
The company reported that profits grew steadily despite the strike.
Looking back, the war lasted much longer than anyone expected.
